title: Sec. 11.1-2. - Definitions.
text:
Sec. 11.1-2. - Definitions.
The following words, terms, and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Authorized Agent. The person or company that is available on a 24-hours-a-day, seven-days-a-week basis and who has been registered with the Town of Clayton as being authorized to accept service for any landlord of any inquiry, notice, complaint or violation regarding the health, safety and/or condition of a rental unit. In the event that a landlord is a nonresident individual or foreign artificial entity, then a registered agent shall serve as the authorized agent but only so long as that person or company is available in the State of Delaware or within a 50-mile radius of the incorporated Town of Clayton 24-hours-a-day, seven-days-a-week basis to address any inquiry, notice, complaint, or violation regarding the health, safety, and/or condition of the rental unit.
Authorized Person. A person, friend, or family member not receiving exchange of money for profit, not in business through the State of Delaware that oversees the responsibility of the property on the owner's behalf and is approved by the property owner. This person is required to be available on a 24-hours-a-day, seven-days-a-week basis as being authorized to accept service for any inquiry, notice, complaint, or violation regarding the health, safety, and/or condition of a rental unit. The "authorized person" is the main contact in the event the property owner is not available within a 50-mile radius of the Town of Clayton.
Department. The Department of Inspections and Enforcement of the Town of Clayton and all designated employees or any successor department or division that may be established.
Drug-related criminal activity. The illegal manufacture, sale, distribution, use, or possession of any illegal or controlled substance defined by Delaware Title 16 chapter 47. as the same may be amended from time to time and in accordance with any future corresponding provision of law.
Dwelling Unit. A single unit providing complete, independent living facilities for one or more persons, including permanent provisions for living, sleeping, eating, cooking, and sanitation.
Improvement. A change or addition to the original approved structure or land that increases its value.
Landlord. The owner, lessor, or sublessor of a rental unit or a managing agent for the owner, or any person authorized to exercise any management of a rental unit, including any person who is authorized to receive any rent or any part of the rent, other than as a bona fide purchaser, and who has no obligation to deliver any portion of that rent to another. It also shall mean any person held out by the owner or the landlord as the appropriate person to accept performance or any person with whom the tenant normally deals as a landlord.
Owner. Any person, agent, operator, firm, or corporation having a legal or equitable interest in a property or recorded in the official records of the state, county, or municipality as holding title to the property or otherwise having control of the property, including the guardian of the estate of any such person, and the executor or administrator of the estate of such person if ordered to take possession of real property by a court.
Owner Occupied Rental Unit. A rental unit that is occupied in whole or in part by an individual whose name specifically appears on the deed for the property where the rental unit is located.
Person. An individual, corporation, partnership, or any other group acting as a unit.
Premises. A lot, plot, or parcel of land, including the buildings or structures thereon.
Rental Property Registration Form. An application provided by the Town of Clayton that must be completed for each rental unit that is subject to regulation pursuant to this article.
Rental Unit. That portion of any house, dwelling unit, dwelling place, building, or structure that is occupied, rented, or leased as the home or residence of one or more persons to the exclusion of all others.
Residential Rental Property. The entire property on or in which any rental unit is located. By definition, every residential rental property must contain at least one rental unit.
Short-Term Rental. A residential property or a portion thereof that is rented or leased to guests for a period of less than 30 consecutive days. This type of rental arrangement is often facilitated through platforms such as Airbnb, VRBO, or similar services and typically involves the temporary provision of lodging accommodations.
Tenant. A person, corporation, partnership, or group, whether or not the legal owner of record, occupying a building or portion thereof as a unit.
(Ord. No. 2024-17, 9-5-2024)

title: Sec. 4.1-3. - Junk yards.
text:
Sec. 4.1-3. - Junk yards.
4.1-3.1
It shall be unlawful to maintain a place for the buying, selling, or storing of junk, scrap, salvage, or any other waste or obsolete material within the Town. Any person, corporation, or entity convicted for a violation of this article shall be fined $100.00 for the first offense and $200.00 for each subsequent offense. Each day of a continuing violation constitutes a separate offense.

title: Sec. 3.3-1. - Traffic, parking, and vehicles.
text:
Sec. 3.3-1. - Traffic, parking, and vehicles.
3.3-1.1
Stopping, standing, or parking in specific places.
a.
No person shall stop, stand, or park a vehicle except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or traffic controlled device in any of the following places:
(1)
On a sidewalk.
(2)
In front of a public or private driveway.
(3)
Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
(4)
On a crosswalk.
(5)
Within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.
(6)
Within 30 feet upon the approach to any flashing beacon, stop sign, or traffic control signal located at the side of the roadway.
(7)
Within 20 feet of the driveway entrance to any fire station and on the side of a street opposite the entrance to any fire station within 75 feet of the entrance when properly sign posted.
(8)
Alongside or opposite any street excavation or obstruction when such stopping, standing, or parking a vehicle would obstruct traffic.
(9)
On the roadway side of any vehicle stopped or parked at the edge or curb of a street.
(10)
At any place where official signs prohibit stopping, standing, or parking.
(11)
Within 50 feet of the nearest rail or railroad crossing unless a different length is indicated by traffic control devices.
(12)
At any place where such parking, standing, or stopping obstructs the free passage of other traffic.
(13)
Upon the roadway of any highway when it is practical to stop, stand, or park off the roadway.
(14)
Whenever a curb is marked yellow or a yellow line is placed at the edge of a roadway or shoulder.
b.
No person shall move a vehicle not owned by such person into any area prohibited under subsection (a) of this section or away from a curb such as is unlawful.
3.3-1.2
Handicap parking.
a.
Definitions. The following words, terms, and phrases when used in this section shall have the meaning ascribed to them in this subsection except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning.
"Vehicle" of the handicapped means a vehicle which is displaying a special handicapped registration plate on the rear of the vehicle issued pursuant to Title 21 Delaware Code § 2134 (or any future corresponding provision of law), a vehicle displaying a special handicapped ID parking card in the windshield such ID card issued pursuant to Title 21 Delaware Code §2135 (or any future corresponding provision of law), or a plate or permit issued under a similar provision in another jurisdiction.
b.
Prohibited conduct. No person shall park any vehicle other than a vehicle of the handicapped in any area under the control of and designated by the State Department of Transportation, by the Town, or by the owner(s) or lessee(s) of private property in the Town as a handicapped parking zone and conspicuously marked as such.
3.3-1.3
Parking in fire lanes.
a.
Prohibited conduct. No person shall stop, stand, or park a vehicle in any place which has been designated and properly identified as a fire lane pursuant to regulations of the State Fire Marshall or in an area designed for a fire hydrant or standpipe connection except in compliance with the directions of a police officer or traffic control device.
b.
Enforcement by towing. Any police officer in the Town is hereby authorized to remove or cause to be removed and stored at the owner's expense any unattended vehicle left standing wholly or partially within a fire lane or any unattended vehicle left standing in a location so as to cause an obstruction to the accessibility to a fire lane, fire hydrant, or standpipe connection.
3.3-1.4
Positioning of vehicle: obedience of markings. all vehicles are hereby required to be parked on the streets of the town according to street markings designated for that purpose, and on the streets that are not marked all vehicles are required to park parallel to and not more than 12 inches from the curb to the right side of the street.
3.3-1.5
Parking of trucks and other heavy equipment. No person shall park or allow to remain parked any truck, mobile heavy construction equipment, or other vehicles licensed by this state or any other state as a commercial vehicle in excess of 1 ton on any public street, road, alley, or way within the limits of Town except as provided in subsequent sections of this article. For purposes of this section, "park" shall mean to bring a vehicle to a stop and leave remaining in 1 place in excess of 5 minutes.
3.3-1.6
Parking prohibited during certain hours. It shall be unlawful for any person to park or allow to remain parked any motor vehicle on a street at the time designated by signage for sweeping of said street by the Town of Clayton or its designee.
3.3-1.7
Parking prohibited in certain areas at all times. It shall be unlawful to park any vehicle at any time in the following areas:
a.
Cherry Alley.
b.
Peach Alley.
c.
Apple Alley.
d.
Pear Alley.
e.
Plum Alley.
f.
State Alley.
g.
Church Alley.
h.
Apricot Alley.
3.3-1.8
Time designated parking. No person shall park in any time designated parking space beyond the designated time.
3.3-1.9
Reserved.
3.3-1.10
Reserved.
3.3-1.11
Liability for costs> The registered owner of a towed vehicle shall be responsible for payment in full of all removal and storage costs absent a decision by a court of applicable jurisdiction that no probable cause existed for towing.
3.3-1.12
Disposition of vehicles following payment of costs. Subsequent to a decision by the court of applicable jurisdiction that probable cause existed for towing or in the absence of a request for a hearing by the registered owner following proper notice, the Town police department shall release the vehicle to the registered owner or to a person legally entitled to its possession upon payment in full of all removal and storage costs and upon a showing of proof of ownership or proof of the right to possession of the vehicle.
3.3-1.13
Penalty and fines.
a.
Any person convicted of violating this article shall be deemed guilty of a violation, and upon conviction before any court of competent jurisdiction shall be penalized as follows:
(1)
First Offense .....$10.00
(2)
Second Offense .....$25.00
(3)
Third Offense .....$50.00
b.
For purposes of determining whether a violation of this article is a second, third, or subsequent offense, only violations occurring within 180 days immediately prior to the violation in question and resulting in convictions will be counted.
c.
Each day that a violation of this article or any provision thereof continues shall be considered as a separate offense and penalties shall be imposed accordingly.
3.3-1.14
Miscellaneous parking.
a.
No boat, boat trailer, utility trailer, RV, camper, or off-highway vehicle (OHV) shall be stored, parked, placed or maintained on any public roadway, street or other public property for a period of time exceeding 72 hours.
b.
Roll-off dumpsters or portable storage containers. Roll-off dumpsters or portable storage containers for the purpose of remodeling, storage, cleanup of debris, etc., shall not be placed, stored, or maintained as to interfere with moving traffic, the obstruction of a motor vehicle operator, private parking and residential parking spaces, or in violation of the traffic laws of the Town of Clayton or State of Delaware. Roll-off dumpsters or portable storage containers shall not be placed, stored, or maintained for a period longer than two weeks.
3.3-1.15
Scope/enforcement. The parking regulations in this article shall be in full force and effect at all times, and the Town's police department is authorized and empowered to install any necessary signs or symbols clearly setting forth the areas mentioned in this section as a no parking zone.
(Ord. of 4-8-2019; Ord. No. 202318, 11-13-2023; Ord. No. 2024-10, 5-22-2024; Ord. No. 2025-04, 3-21-2025)

title: Sec. 2.3-6. - Required inspection and certification of dams and stormwater management structures.
text:
Sec. 2.3-6. - Required inspection and certification of dams and stormwater management structures.
2.3-6.1
Purpose. The purpose of this ordinance [from which this section derived] is to ensure the structural integrity, functionality, and public safety of privately owned dams, stormwater ponds, and outlet structures within the Town of Clayton. Proper routine inspection and certification are essential to prevent hazards, mitigate liability, and ensure compliance with best management practices.
2.3-6.2
Definitions. The following words, terms, and phrases, when used in this Article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Dam. Any artificial barrier constructed for the purpose of impounding or storing water;
Stormwater Pond. A man-made basin designed to collect, manage, and treat stormwater runoff, including detention basins, retention basins, dry ponds, and wet ponds;
Spillway. A structure designed to safely convey excess water from a dam or pond to downstream areas;
Outlet Structure. A riser, pipe, weir, or other mechanism regulating the release of water from a stormwater pond or dam;
Stormwater Management Facility. Any infrastructure used to manage stormwater runoff, including dams, ponds, spillways, and outlet structures;
Homeowners Association (HOA) and Maintenance Corporations. An entity responsible for managing and maintaining common property within a residential community;
Qualified Engineer. A professional engineer licensed in the State of Delaware with relevant experience in dam safety, stormwater management, or hydrology.
2.3-6.3
Applicability. This ordinance applies to all dams, stormwater ponds, outlet structures, and other stormwater management facilities within the Town of Clayton that are owned, operated, or maintained by a homeowner's association (HOA), maintenance corporation, or any other legal entity. This includes new and existing structures not otherwise subject to state or federal oversight.
2.3-6.4
Right to inspect. The Town of Clayton, through its officers, employees, agents, and otherwise authorized designees, reserves the right to inspect any dam, stormwater facility, or associated property at any time, with or without advance notice, to ensure compliance with this ordinance [from which this section derived] or to assess potential threats to public health and safety.
2.3-6.5
Classifications.
a.
Dam Hazzard Classification.
(1)
Dams shall be classified in accordance with the federal hazard classification system:
(i)
Class I—High Hazard Potential. Dams where failure or improper operation would likely cause probable loss of human life. Residential areas or recreational sites downstream imply this classification;
(ii)
Class II—Significant Hazard Potential. Dams where failure may cause possible loss of life, economic loss, environmental harm, or utility disruption. Applies to rural areas or sites affecting roads, homes, or public services;
(iii)
Class III—Low Hazard Potential. Dams unlikely to cause loss of life but which may result in minor economic or environmental losses, typically in rural or agricultural areas.
Class III dams are exempt from inspection and certification requirements under this ordinance [from which this section derived] unless reclassified by a licensed Delaware engineer and accepted by the Town of Clayton.
2.3-6.6
Dam Inspection and Certification Requirements.
a.
Annual Inspection. All applicable dams must be inspected annually by a qualified Delaware engineer approved by the Town of Clayton. The Town reserves the right to require more frequent inspections or impose additional conditions for Class I and II due to increased risk levels. Inspection reports must be submitted to the Code Official within 30 days of completion. The inspection shall include but shall not be limited to:
(1)
Structural stability;
(2)
Embankment and spillway integrity;
(3)
Signs of erosion, sediment buildup, or vegetation issues;
(4)
Blockages or obstructions; and
(5)
Maintenance recommendations.
b.
Certification Every Five Years. Every five years, a full certification must be completed by a licensed Delaware engineer stating that the facility is:
(1)
Structurally sound;
(2)
Functioning as designed; and
(3)
Compliant with local and federal safety standards.
If deficiencies are found, a corrective action plan must be submitted within 60 days.
c.
Quarterly Visual Inspections for Class I and II Dams. All Class I (High Hazard) and Class II (Significant Hazard) dams must be visually inspected quarterly by an owner-designated representative. These inspections shall at minimum check for:
(1)
Erosion;
(2)
Woody-stemmed vegetation, invasive growth or overgrown riparian buffers;
(3)
Sediment accumulation;
(4)
Blockages to water flow or outlet structures; vegetation growing through the dam; and
(5)
Changes in the spillway conditions.
A log of each visual inspection must be maintained by the responsible owner and made available to the Town upon request. If deficiencies are found, corrective action must be taken within 30 days.
2.6-6.7
Stormwater Pond Inspection and Certification Requirements.
a.
All stormwater ponds must be visually inspected quarterly by an HOA-designated representative. These inspections shall check for:
(1)
Erosion;
(2)
Woody-stemmed vegetation or invasive growth;
(3)
Sediment accumulation;
(4)
Blockages to water flow or outlet structures; and
(5)
Changes in the spillway.
A log of each visual inspection must be maintained by the HOA and made available to the municipality upon request.
b.
Annual Visual Inspection. All stormwater ponds must be visually inspected once per year by the property owner or designee. The purpose of the inspection is to ensure the pond is functioning as designed and not presenting a hazard to public health, safety, or the environment. Records must be submitted to the Code Official within 30 days of completion. The visual inspection must include an assessment of:
(1)
Embankments. Check for signs of erosion, cracking, animal burrows, settlement, or slumping;
(2)
Inlets and Outlets. Ensure inlets are not blocked by debris and outlets are not clogged, damaged, or obstructed;
(3)
Spillways. Examine primary and emergency spillways for erosion, sedimentation, overgrowth, or structural damage;
(4)
Vegetation. Look for overgrown or woody vegetation that could obstruct flow or damage structures; ensure grass is well-maintained;
(5)
Sediment Accumulation. Check for excessive sediment in forebays or pond bottoms that may reduce storage or treatment capacity;
(6)
Standing Water. Ensure water levels are appropriate and not stagnant for extended periods unless part of the design (e.g., wet ponds); and
(7)
Safety Hazards. Identify broken fencing, steep drop-offs, or other safety concerns.
c.
Five-Year Engineer Certification. Every five years, a Delaware-licensed engineer must certify that each stormwater pond is:
(1)
Free of structural defects;
(2)
Free of obstructions; and
(3)
Operating in accordance with its design and stormwater permits.
Deficiencies must be addressed through a corrective action plan within 60 days.
2.3-6.8
Water Level Management.
a.
In anticipation of severe weather, flood events, or any other emergency, the Town of Clayton reserves the right to require the temporary lowering of the water level in any dam or stormwater management facility deemed at risk to downstream properties or public safety. Furthermore:
(1)
Such a directive may be issued by the Town Manager, Mayor or other authorized official, based on weather forecasts, site conditions, or risk assessments;
(2)
Responsible owners shall comply with this directive within the timeframe specified by the Town; and
(3)
Failure to comply with a water level adjustment order may result in municipal intervention to enforce compliance, with all associated costs charged to the responsible owner.
b.
Coordination and Approval of Water Level Lowering. No homeowners' association (HOA), officer, agent, or member thereof, or other responsible party shall lower the water level of any dam or stormwater management facility without prior coordination with, and written approval from, the Town of Clayton. All such lowering of water levels shall be conducted in accordance with specifications, methods, and timeframes prescribed by the Town.
c.
Emergency Provision. In the event of an immediate and demonstrable danger to the health, welfare, or safety to the people and property of the Town of Clayton, an homeowners' association (HOA) or other responsible party may initiate an emergency lowering of the water level without prior written approval; however, the Town must be notified of such action immediately and no later than 30 minutes after commencement. The responsible party shall provide the Town with the reason for the emergency lowering, the anticipated extent of the water level reduction, and the estimated timeframe for restoration to normal levels. Any lowering of water levels under this provision shall be limited to the extent necessary to address the immediate danger and shall be subject to any stipulations that the Town may prescribe.
2.3-6.9
Reporting and Recordkeeping.
a.
All engineering reports, certifications, and visual inspection logs must be retained by the responsible owner and submitted to the municipality as required.
b.
The Town of Clayton reserves the right to conduct site visits and request supplemental documentation or re-inspection if needed.
2.3-6.10
Enforcement and Penalties. Failure to comply with this ordinance [from which this section derived] may result in any of the following or combination thereof:
a.
A fine up to $100.00 per day of noncompliance;
b.
Suspension of Town approvals or services for noncompliant facilities; and/or
c.
Town of Clayton action to inspect or repair at the HOA's expense, in cases of imminent public safety concerns.
d.
Any violation of Section 2.3-6.8(b) or (c) shall be subject to a fine not to exceed $1,000.00, which shall be assessed based on the extent of damage caused to any person(s), property(s), and/or infrastructure by said unauthorized lowering; in addition to any other municipal, civil or criminal penalty—subject to applicable law.
2.3-6.11
Exemptions and Thresholds. This ordinance does not apply to:
a.
Stormwater ponds impounding less than 0.25 acre-feet and embankments under three feet high;
b.
Facilities under state or federal dam safety programs with equal or stricter requirements; or
c.
Class III (Low Hazard) dams, unless reclassified by a licensed Delaware engineer due to increased risk.
2.3-6.12
Severability. If any provision or section of this ordinance [from which this section derived] is deemed invalid, unconstitutional or unenforceable by a court of competent jurisdiction, the remaining provisions shall remain in full force and effect.
(Ord. No. 2025-11, 9-15-2025)
